findings.title: BAT_ENABLE via (17.1,82.8) to BAT_FAULT_N is 0.173 mm on 1407e850, not 0.200 mm; docs call it re-measured and unchanged
findings.contradicts: M3_R10.md lines 292 and 306-307 ('the ... BAT_FAULT_N clearances below were re-measured on 1407e850... and are unchanged'; 'the BAT_ENABLE via (17.1,82.8) to BAT_FAULT_N 0.200 mm'); R10_VALIDATION.md line 2252 (§1 inventory for PCB 1407e850: '0.200 mm ... Inside U9's fan-out; not changed') and line 2092 (owner row 24: '0.200 mm from BAT_FAULT_N ... fixed by ... U9's fan-out and stay'); FMEA_REDUNDANCY.md line 36 (H-6: 'the BAT_ENABLE via to BAT_FAULT_N 0.200 mm'); ORDERING.md line 570 (coating worksheet: 'the (17.1,82.8) via 0.200 mm from BAT_FAULT_N')
findings.evidence: pcbnew shape clearance on m3_design/assembly_review/m3.kicad_pcb (sha 1407e850...): BAT_ENABLE via (17.10,82.80) 0.5/0.3 mm on F.Cu to the BAT_FAULT_N F.Cu track (16.55,82.99)-(16.91,83.35), width 0.20 mm: 0.1733 mm (segment-to-centre distance minus half widths; probe .supervisor/r24_docs_binding/tr.py and clr.py). On 5516eeec (git show 9b27268) the same run turned a 90-degree corner at (16.55,83.35) and the gap was 0.200 mm; the D-R24-17 chamfer added the diagonal that brings it to 0.173 mm. DRC still passes (0.15 mm floor).
findings.impact: The safety inventory, owner row 24, the FMEA and the coating worksheet state a gap that the current board does not have, and M3_R10 says it was re-measured unchanged. The leak-threshold arithmetic (0.58 Mohm latch) does not depend on the gap, so no calculation changes.
findings.concrete_fix: Replace 0.200 mm with 0.173 mm (F.Cu, chamfer segment (16.55,82.99)-(16.91,83.35), since D-R24-17) in the five places; drop 'unchanged' for this pair in M3_R10 line 292 and 'not changed' in R10_VALIDATION line 2252.

findings.title: ORDERING 8.2 says 14 pin legends are on the bottom; its own list and the board have 13
findings.contradicts: ORDERING.md line 416: '14 pin legends are on the bottom beside their pins (R23-DOCS_BINDING-09): J121 2:E1+, J400 2:SW, J440 2:GND / 3:TXO / 4:RXI, J410 2:GND / 3:TXO, J420 2:GND / 3:TXO, J9 2:GND / 3:RXI and J122 2:S2 / 4:S4'
findings.evidence: The enumerated list has 1+1+3+2+2+2+2 = 13 entries. B.Silkscreen board texts (probe silk.py): 2:E1+ (4.0,57.6), 2:GND (4.1,14.0), 4:RXI (4.2,21.5), 2:SW (4.4,67.6), 3:TXO (10.5,17.5), 2:S2 (41.3,74.5), 3:RXI (41.5,45.25), 3:TXO (41.7,13.25), 3:TXO (41.7,29.25), 2:GND (41.9,16.75 / 32.75 / 48.75), 4:S4 (40.4,67.2) = 13 terminal pin legends; the other 5 bottom texts are J2's four pin legends and M3-ASSY-R10. Top has 14 terminal pin legends; 14 + 13 = 27 contacts, as M3_R10 states.
findings.impact: The pin-identity inspection count is wrong (an inspector looking for 14 bottom legends finds 13).
findings.concrete_fix: Change '14 pin legends' to '13 pin legends' in ORDERING.md line 416.

findings.title: round24_board_cad record calls the orientation-reconstruction counts 'rows per side' of the CPL
findings.contradicts: round24_board_cad.md line 56 (CPL bullet: 'Rows per side go from 69 top + 122 bottom to 67 + 125') and round24_board_cad.json manufacturing.cpl.sides ('69 top + 122 bottom -> 67 top + 125 bottom'); M3_R10.md 'The board' (206 CPL rows, 70 top + 136 bottom)
findings.evidence: fab/m3_cpl_jlc.csv at f2b8251: 70 Top + 136 Bottom rows (206); at 9b27268: 72 Top + 133 Bottom (205). 67 + 125 (and 69 + 122 before) are jlc_orient --verify-cpl's reconstructed parts, which exclude the 14 placement-only rows (run read-only: '67 top and 125 bottom rows rebuilt ... placement-only checks: 14 ... expected rows: 206').
findings.impact: The board-pass record misstates the CPL's per-side row counts (it would mislead a reader checking JLC's upload, 70 / 136).
findings.concrete_fix: Write 'CPL rows per side 72 + 133 -> 70 + 136; orientation reconstruction 69 + 122 -> 67 + 125 (+ 14 placement-only)' in the .md and the JSON 'sides' field.
